recipes.title: Roasted Salmon & Veg Traybake
recipes.note: Recipe as written serves 4; halved here. Lemon and garlic don't halve cleanly — use a whole lemon and a small pinch of garlic to taste.
method: Preheat the oven to 200ºC/400ºF/gas 6.
Cook the potatoes in boiling salted water for 10-12 minutes until cooked through, adding the green beans for the final 2 minutes. Drain.
Tip the veg into a bowl, halve and add the tomatoes, destone and add the olives along with half the basil leaves. Add a little olive oil, toss and tip into a roasting tray.

Toss the salmon fillets with a little olive oil and a squeeze of lemon juice, season lightly. Lay on top of the vegetables skin-side up, top with a couple of lemon slices, and roast for 10 minutes until cooked through.

For the yoghurt: bash the remaining basil with a pinch of salt, add the garlic and bash again. Mix in the mustard, Greek yoghurt and remaining lemon juice, plus a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil. Season to taste and serve with the salmon traybake.

recipes.title: Lemony Courgette Linguine
method: Cook the linguine in boiling salted water according to packet instructions. Drain, reserving a mugful of cooking water.
Slice the courgettes lengthways, then into long matchsticks (or use the julienne cutter on a mandolin).
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the courgettes and cook for 4 minutes, tossing regularly. Finely slice the mint leaves and stir in.
Toss the drained pasta into the pan with a splash of reserved cooking water. Finely grate in most of the Parmesan and a little lemon zest, squeeze in all the juice. Toss well, taste and season.
Dish up, grate over the remaining Parmesan and drizzle with 1 tsp extra virgin olive oil.

recipes.title: Quick Sticky Chicken Salad
recipes.note: Recipe as written serves 4; halved here.

ingredients.item: Zest of 1/2 lemon and juice of 3/4 lemon
Small bunch fresh mint, half chopped, half kept whole
skinless chicken breasts, each sliced into 3 pieces
garlic ciabatta, sliced in half lengthways
tinned chickpeas, drained and rinsed (half a 400g tin)

method: Mix together the lemon zest and juice (keeping about 1 tbsp juice back for the dressing), honey, 1 tbsp of the oil and the chopped mint. Season and add the chicken, stir to coat, leave 10 minutes.
Blanch the broad beans in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain, refresh in cold water, drain again and slip from their skins. Tear the ciabatta into pieces and grill for 5 minutes until golden.
Heat a griddle over high heat. Cook chicken 2-3 minutes each side until charred, sticky and cooked through.

Toss the lettuce, broad beans, ciabatta, chickpeas, tomatoes, cucumber, parsley and remaining mint in a large bowl. Whisk the remaining oil, 1 tbsp lemon juice and mustard into a dressing. Season, pour over, add the warm chicken and toss.

recipes.title: Pan-Roasted Pork Tenderloin with Fennel
method: Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F.
Pat the pork dry with paper towel. Rub ground fennel seeds all over the meat, season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the tenderloin on all sides, about 6 minutes. Remove and set aside on a plate.
Cut fennel bulbs into 1.5cm wedges. Using the same pan, sauté fennel and garlic over medium heat until fennel is golden and tender, about 6 minutes.
Add wine and deglaze the pan, scraping up any brown bits. Add butter and broth; stir to combine.
Place pork on top of the fennel and transfer the pan to the oven. Roast until the internal temperature reaches 63–65°C, about 15 minutes.
Transfer pork to a cutting board and rest for 10 minutes.
While pork rests, return the skillet to the stovetop and simmer the liquid until almost completely reduced.
Add lemon juice, reduce heat, and stir in the reserved chopped fennel fronds.
Slice pork, serve over fennel wedges, and spoon sauce over the top.
notes: Use an instant-read thermometer — 63°C keeps the pork juicy. Don't skip the rest.

recipes.title: Sea Bass Crudo
recipes.note: Serves 2 as a starter. No cooking required.

ingredients.item: sea bass fillets, skinned and pin-boned
Flaky sea salt and black pepper

method: Place the fish and your serving plates in the freezer for 10 minutes beforehand — cold fish slices more cleanly and stays fresher longer on the plate.
Using a sharp knife, slice the fish thinly on a 45° angle, about 2–3mm thick. Lay slices in a single layer on the cold plates.
Sprinkle with flaky salt, then drizzle lemon juice over the fish, followed by the olive oil.
Crack over black pepper and add any optional garnishes.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ask your fishmonger to skin and pin-bone the sea bass for you. Quality of fish is everything here — buy the freshest you can find.

recipes.title: Perfect Pan-Fried Chicken Breasts

ingredients.item: anchovy fillet, drained (or 1/2 tsp chopped capers)
Small handful parsley or chives, chopped

method: Put the chicken breasts in a large food bag and bash the thicker parts with a rolling pin until an even 1.5-1.7cm thick. Add the salt and massage into the chicken. Leave at room temperature to dry-brine for 30 minutes (no more).

Remove from the bag and brush off excess salt. Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat, add the oil. Once simmering, add the chicken. Cook 5-6 minutes each side without moving it, for a strong caramelised sear. In the final minute, add the butter and baste the chicken once it's foaming. Rest the chicken 5 minutes.

While resting, add the anchovy to the butter in the pan, stirring until dissolved. Add the vinegar, swirl and cook 1 minute. Slice the chicken against the grain, plate up, add resting juices to the sauce with the chopped herbs, and pour over the chicken.
notes: The original recipe suggests roast new potatoes and seasonal veg as sides — swap in boiled new potatoes or a simple summer salad to keep it fully oven-free in hot weather.

recipes.title: Lamb Cutlets in Basil Sauce

ingredients.item: Small handful fresh thyme, leaves picked
mushrooms, brushed clean and torn (wild, or chestnut/oyster)

method: Best cooked on a hot barbecue, or use a preheated ridged griddle/frying pan. Flatten the cutlets slightly. Bash the thyme with a little olive oil in a pestle and mortar, rub over the cutlets, and season both sides.

Cook the mushrooms dry on the hot pan, both sides, to mark them, then set aside in a large bowl. Cook the lamb: about 3-4 minutes each side for cutlets around 1.5cm thick, for medium (less time for rare).
Add the lamb to the mushroom bowl, drizzle with olive oil, tear over the parsley, squeeze over the lemon juice, season, and toss. Rest so the juices soak into the mushrooms.

Make the sauce: pound the pine nuts to a pulp in a pestle and mortar, transfer to a bowl. Pound the basil to a pulp and add to the pine nuts, loosening with olive oil until it drops easily off a spoon.
Balance with balsamic vinegar to taste for a good zing. Give the lamb and mushrooms a final toss. Serve on a platter with the sauce and a simple watercress salad on the side.

recipes.title: Thai Basil Chicken (Pad Kra Pao Gai)
recipes.note: Hob only — no oven. Recipe as written serves 1; doubled here for 2. Andy prefers milder heat than the traditional version — start with 2-3 chillies rather than the 8 below, or deseed them.

ingredients.item: chicken breasts, cut into small bite-sized pieces (about 400g)
Thai chillies — start with 2-3 for less heat (see note)
Thai holy basil leaves (Thai sweet basil as a substitute)

method: Get a pot of jasmine rice on so it's ready when the chicken is.

Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a wok or frying pan over high heat. Fry the eggs one at a time, splashing hot oil over the yolk as it cooks, until crisp at the edges and the yolk is still runny. Drain and set aside.
Pound or finely chop the garlic and chillies together — just enough to bring out the oils, no need for a paste. Pluck the basil leaves from their stems.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in the wok over high heat. Add the garlic and chillies and stir-fry about 20 seconds until fragrant, without burning.
Add the chicken and stir-fry continuously until just cooked through, 2-3 minutes. Add a splash of water if the pan looks dry.
Add the oyster sauce, light soy sauce, sugar and dark soy sauce. Stir-fry another 30 seconds.
Add the basil, fold it through, and take off the heat immediately — it only needs a few seconds to wilt.
Serve over the rice with a fried egg on the side.
notes: Holy basil (bai kra prao) has a peppery flavour and is the authentic choice. Thai sweet basil works as a substitute but loses that peppery note.
Pairs well with an off-dry Riesling — the fruit and acidity balance the chilli heat and salty sauce.

recipes.title: Roast Turbot with Leeks, Tarragon and Riesling
recipes.note: Recipe as written serves 3-4 off a 1.2-1.5kg turbot; halved here for 2 — pairs with Rockfish's Whole Turbot for Two (600g). Leeks and lemon don't halve perfectly cleanly — rounded up to 2 leeks and half a lemon's juice.

ingredients.item: leeks, outer leaves removed and washed

method: Heat the oven to 180°C fan/gas 6. Finely slice the spring onions and fennel, then cut the leeks into 3cm chunks. Melt the butter in a large flameproof roasting dish over medium heat, add the veg, season well with salt and pepper, and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened (8-10 minutes).

Pour in the Riesling, stir through, then turn off the heat. Lay the turbot on top of the vegetables, white skin side down, and make 2 slashes across its back. Season with a pinch of salt and roast for 15-18 minutes — it's ready when a milky liquid appears in the slashes.

Scatter over the tarragon leaves and squeeze over the lemon juice. Bring the dish to the table and carve — there are 4 fillets on a turbot: lift the first 2 off the top, then flip and remove the 2 underneath.
notes: Wine pairing: an oaked white Rioja or a mature white Burgundy — enough depth and structure for the rich, buttery sauce. (Matching Food & Wine)

recipes.title: Beef & Broccoli Stir-Fry
recipes.note: Recipe as written serves 4; halved here. Ginger, chilli and lime don't halve perfectly cleanly — use a smaller piece of ginger, half a chilli, and half a lime to taste.

ingredients.item: Egg noodles or steamed rice, to serve

method: Blanch the broccoli in boiling salted water for 10 minutes; drain.
Finely slice the onion and garlic, chop the ginger, slice the chilli, and cut the lime into wedges.
Pound the coriander seeds with salt and pepper using a pestle and mortar.
Slice the steak into finger-sized strips and coat with the spice mixture.
Heat a wok on high heat; add a little olive oil, then cook the onion, garlic and ginger for 2 minutes.
Add the beef and fry for 2 minutes. Add the broccoli and fry for a further 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the soy sauce and sesame oil; toss to coat.
Serve with egg noodles or steamed rice, topped with the remaining chilli and a squeeze of lime juice.

recipes.title: Pan-Fried Cod with Prawn & Lemon Butter
recipes.note: Recipe as written serves 4; halved here.

ingredients.item: lemon, finely grated rind and juice
spinach leaves, lightly steamed, to serve

method: Coat the cod with the seasoned flour. Heat the oil and half the butter in a large frying pan until foaming. Add the cod and fry for 4 minutes per side until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Wipe the pan clean. Add the remaining butter and heat until melted. Add the prawns and lemon rind, warming gently for 20-30 seconds, then stir in the lemon juice.
Serve the cod with the steamed spinach and pour over the lemon-prawn butter. Season with freshly ground black pepper.
notes: Can be made with another white fish, such as haddock, if you prefer.

recipes.title: Creamy Lemon-Tarragon Chicken Orzo with Feta & Mint
recipes.note: Not a sourced recipe — a one-off built from what was in the fridge/pantry that day. Not keto (orzo).

ingredients.item: chicken breasts, cut into bite-size pieces

method: Season the chicken. Heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and sear the chicken until golden and just cooked through. Set aside.
In the same pan, soften the shallot, garlic and carrot for a few minutes.
Stir in the orzo and toast for a minute, then add the stock. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until the orzo is al dente and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Return the chicken to the pan with the chopped tarragon. Take off the heat and stir through the Greek yogurt (off the heat so it doesn't split).
Finish with crumbled feta, chopped mint, black pepper, and lemon juice/zest if using.
notes: Swap the yogurt finish for an egg-lemon (avgolemono) enrichment for a more traditionally Greek technique — whisk eggs with lemon juice, temper with hot cooking liquid, then stir through off the heat instead of the yogurt.

recipes.title: Salmon, Green Beans and Edamame
recipes.note: Adapted: no sugar in the dressing, and the peas swapped for extra green beans to keep it strictly keto.

ingredients.item: large limes (1 juiced, 1 cut into wedges)
fresh mint leaves, finely chopped, plus extra to garnish
small red chilli, deseeded and finely chopped
fine green beans, trimmed and halved

method: Whisk together the oil, lime juice, mint and chilli; season and set aside.
Spread the sesame seeds on a plate. Season the salmon with pepper, then coat in the seeds.

Heat the remaining oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Fry the salmon for 1.5-2 minutes per side until golden, then lower the heat and cook for 2 minutes more until done. Rest on a warm plate.
Steam the green beans and mangetout for 5-6 minutes until tender. Toss with two-thirds of the dressing.
Plate the vegetables, top with the salmon, and drizzle over the remaining dressing. Serve with lime wedges and mint.
notes: Net carbs worked out from per-ingredient USDA data on 2026-09-20 (~14g with the original peas). Mangetout and lime juice figures are unverified estimates. The source page's own nutrition panel was replaced with figures worked out from the adapted ingredients — it described the version with peas.

Energy, protein and fat estimated from per-ingredient USDA data on 2026-09-26. Herbs, spices and citrus juice not counted (under ~15 kcal a serving). Weights assumed where the recipe gives none (chicken breasts ~150g each, courgettes ~200g each).
recipes.nutritionNote: per serving, estimated from the ingredients as adapted

recipes.title: Fennel & Mascarpone Risotto with Scallops and Prosciutto
recipes.note: Weekend risotto, chosen to go with a full-bodied, mineral white (white Burgundy). Not keto.

ingredients.item: fresh scallops (diver-caught if possible), corals detached

method: Soften the base — Melt the butter in a large, deep frying pan over a medium-low heat. Add the onion and cook gently for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and fennel and cook for 5 minutes more.
Toast the rice — Stir in the rice until coated, pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2–3 minutes.

Add the stock — Add the hot stock a few ladlefuls at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed. Keep going for about 20 minutes at a gentle simmer, until the rice is al dente but creamy. Season, cover and rest for 2–3 minutes.

Prosciutto and scallops — Heat the oil in a heavy-based frying pan. Fry the prosciutto for 1 minute until crisp and lift out with tongs. When the pan is hot, season the white parts of the scallops and cook for 1 minute on each side until lightly golden. Add the corals and cook for 30 seconds, then take off the heat.
Finish — Stir the parsley and mascarpone into the risotto. Divide between 2 bowls and top with the crispy prosciutto, scallops and corals. Season with black pepper.
notes: Recipe as written serves 4 — halved here for 2. Half a small onion is what the maths gives; use a whole small one if you'd rather not have half an onion left over. The oil is kept at 1 tbsp so the pan is properly coated.
Chef's tip from the source: cook the meaty white parts first, then just 'show' the corals to the pan — scallops need very little cooking.

Not keto: roughly 60g of carbs a serving from the rice alone (my estimate). The source's nutrition panel lists 2.7g carbs, which can't be right for a risotto (its other figures don't add up either), so it has been left out.

Wine: a full-bodied mineral white such as a Meursault or a Chablis Premier Cru. Sources say the richer the dish, the fuller the wine it can take, and white Burgundy is safe ground with cream and butter. The scallop match is inference from that, not a sourced pairing of this exact dish.

recipes.title: Sumac Chicken and Green Bean Salad
recipes.note: Adapted: no carrot or pomegranate molasses; extra lemon and a little rocket instead.

ingredients.item: olive oil (1 tsp for the chicken, the rest for the dressing)
sumac, plus a pinch to serve

method: Heat the oven to 220C/fan 200C/gas 7. Coat the chicken breasts with 1 tsp of the oil and season. Mix the sumac and cumin and rub it over the chicken. Put on a baking sheet and roast for 15-20 minutes until cooked through.

Whisk the lemon juice with the remaining oil and season to make the dressing. Blanch the green beans in salted boiling water for 2 minutes, then add the red onion for 5 seconds. Cool both in iced water, drain and dry with kitchen paper.

Toss the beans and onion with most of the dressing. Divide between plates with the rocket. Slice the chicken, lay it on top, drizzle with the rest of the dressing and finish with the dill and a pinch of sumac.
notes: Net carbs worked out from per-ingredient USDA data on 2026-09-20 (roughly 4-5g more with the original carrot). The source page's own nutrition panel was replaced with figures worked out from the adapted ingredients — it described the version with carrot and molasses, and its fibre figure didn't add up.

Energy, protein and fat estimated from per-ingredient USDA data on 2026-09-26. Herbs, spices and citrus juice not counted (under ~15 kcal a serving). Weights assumed where the recipe gives none (chicken breasts ~150g each, courgettes ~200g each).
recipes.nutritionNote: per serving, estimated from the ingredients as adapted

recipes.title: Lamb Steaks with Feta, Tomato and Rosemary
recipes.note: Adapted: no couscous or stock — served on dressed spinach instead.

ingredients.item: lamb leg steaks (about 350g in total), trimmed
A handful of flat-leaf parsley, chopped

method: Heat the grill to high. Season the lamb, put it on a baking sheet and grill for 3 minutes each side.
Scatter the feta, tomatoes and rosemary over the lamb and grill for a few minutes more until sizzling.
Toss the spinach with the olive oil, parsley and a squeeze of lemon juice. Serve the lamb on top.
notes: Net carbs worked out from per-ingredient USDA data on 2026-09-20. The source page's own nutrition panel was replaced with figures worked out from the adapted ingredients — it included the couscous.

Energy, protein and fat estimated from per-ingredient USDA data on 2026-09-26. Herbs, spices and citrus juice not counted (under ~15 kcal a serving). Weights assumed where the recipe gives none (chicken breasts ~150g each, courgettes ~200g each).
recipes.nutritionNote: per serving, estimated from the ingredients as adapted

recipes.title: Rack of Lamb with Pistachio & Parsley Crust
recipes.note: Halved from the original (serves 4). Crust made by hand, no food processor. Chosen for Gesellmann Bela Rex 2022 (Cabernet/Merlot).

ingredients.item: French-trimmed 7-bone rack of lamb, caps, fat and sinews removed
Dijon mustard, for brushing (plus ½ tsp for the dressing)
fresh flat-leaf parsley (about ½ a bunch)
garlic clove, peeled and finely chopped

method: Take the lamb out of the fridge to come to room temperature. Heat the oven to 180°C / gas 4.
Drizzle the rack with olive oil and season generously with salt and pepper.
Sear in a hot frying pan with a little oil and butter for 2–3 minutes, turning until golden all over. Move to a roasting tray and leave to cool.

Make the crust by hand: bash the pistachios in a freezer bag or under a tea towel with a rolling pin, then finish with a knife into small, uneven crumbs. Grate the bread on the coarse side of a grater (or tear and rub it into rough crumbs). Finely chop the parsley, dry it well, and chop the garlic. Mix everything together with the grated nutmeg and a pinch of salt.
Brush the rack generously with mustard, then press the crumb over the top and sides.
Roast for 25 minutes until the crust is crisp. Rest for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, trim the beans and boil in salted water for 6–7 minutes.
Whisk the crushed garlic, ½ tsp mustard, vinegar, extra virgin olive oil and lemon juice. Season to taste and stir in the tarragon.
Drain the beans and toss with the dressing. Carve the lamb into cutlets and serve with the beans.
notes: Original recipe blitzes the crust in a food processor. By hand it comes out a bit coarser, but sticks and crisps fine.
Pairs with Gesellmann Bela Rex 2022 (Burgenland, Cabernet Sauvignon/Merlot) — a fuller red suits rack of lamb (Decanter).
Quantities halved from the original (2 racks, serves 4). Nutmeg, garlic and tarragon are rounded to practical amounts.

recipes.title: Sunday Roast Beef Dinner
recipes.note: Combined from four separate sources (beef, gravy, carrots, Yorkshires) — see notes below for each. Not source-checked for keto.

ingredients.item: small handful mixed fresh herbs (thyme, rosemary, bay, sage)
fat and juices from the beef's roasting tin
sprig fresh rosemary and/or a bay leaf
small sprig fresh thyme, leaves picked

method: Take the beef out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking to bring it to room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 240°C / 220°C fan / Gas 9.
Roughly chop the onion, carrot and celery (skins on) and separate the garlic into unpeeled cloves. Scatter them with the mixed herbs in a roasting tray and drizzle with half the olive oil.
Rub the beef with the remaining oil, season with the salt and pepper, and sit it on top of the vegetable bed.

Put the beef in the oven and immediately turn the heat down to 200°C / 180°C fan / Gas 6. For a ~500g joint, roast for about 30 minutes for medium-rare or 35-40 minutes for medium — check with a meat thermometer (50-52°C for medium-rare, 57-60°C for medium; it rises a few degrees more while resting).

Meanwhile, toss the carrots in a separate tin with the vegetable oil, cumin, mustard and maple syrup. Cover with foil and roast (lower shelf, alongside the beef, or just before/after) for 20 minutes, then uncover and roast a further 10-15 minutes until glazed. Scatter with thyme (and za'atar, if using) before serving.
When the beef is done, transfer it to a board, cover loosely with foil, and rest for 20-25 minutes — a bit longer than the strict minimum, since that's the window the Yorkshires and gravy need.
Turn the oven up to 225°C / 425°F / Gas 9. Pour the vegetable oil into 6 compartments of a muffin tin (about 1cm deep in each) and heat in the oven for 10-15 minutes until sizzling hot.
While the oil heats, whisk the egg, flour, milk and a pinch of salt and pepper into a smooth, light batter.
Carefully pour the batter into the hot oil, filling each compartment a third to halfway. Bake for 12-15 minutes until risen and golden — don't open the oven door while they cook, or they'll deflate.

While the Yorkshires bake, make the gravy: set the beef's roasting tin over medium heat on the hob, spoon off most of the fat, then stir in the flour and rosemary/bay to make a smooth paste. Gradually whisk in the beef stock and simmer for 3-4 minutes until thickened. Season to taste, strain through a sieve, and stir in any juices from the resting beef.
Carve the beef thinly against the grain and serve with the gravy, roast carrots and Yorkshire puddings.
notes: Beef: Jamie Oliver, "Perfect Roast Beef" (jamieoliver.com/recipes/beef-recipes/perfect-roast-beef). As written serves 6 (1.5kg joint) — scaled to 2 (500g). Cooking time doesn't scale linearly with weight — the estimate above is approximate; verify with a meat thermometer.
Gravy: delicious. magazine, "Classic Beef Gravy" (deliciousmagazine.co.uk/recipes/classic-beef-gravy). As written serves 6 — scaled to 2 (roughly a third).

Carrots: delicious. magazine, "Honey and Cumin Roast Carrots" (deliciousmagazine.co.uk/recipes/honey-and-cumin-roast-carrots). As written serves 8 — scaled to 2 (a quarter). Cooks at 180°C, slightly cooler than the beef.

Yorkshire puddings: Jamie Oliver, "Amazing Yorkies" (jamieoliver.com/recipes/eggs/amazing-yorkies). As written makes 12 — halved to make about 6 (2 eggs to 1). Needs the hottest oven of the four (225°C) — best baked while the beef rests.
Not checked against the usual keto constraint — Andy confirmed keto doesn't apply to this meal.

recipes.title: Lamb & Red Wine Stew
recipes.note: Uses 500ml of red wine, a good way to finish an open bottle. Oven-baked, hands-off.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C / gas 4.
Trim the celery and roughly chop. Peel and roughly chop the onions. Peel the carrots, slice lengthways and roughly chop.
Heat a casserole pan on a medium heat. Add the vegetables, bay leaf, rosemary and olive oil and fry for 10 minutes.
Add the lamb and flour.
Pour in the wine and tomatoes, stir well and season with salt and pepper.
Bring to the boil, cover with the lid and cook in the oven for 2 hours 30 minutes until the lamb is tender. Take the lid off for the last 30 minutes, adding a splash of water if it looks dry.
Remove the bay leaf and rosemary stalks, taste and season, then serve.
notes: Jamie's page also gives optional dumplings (250g self-raising flour, 125g cold butter, added for the last 30 minutes) or a mashed potato topping to turn it into a shepherd's pie. Not included here.
Halve everything for 2 (250ml wine). Use a smaller casserole so it doesn't reduce away.
Leftover wine freezes well in ice cube trays for later sauces.
recipes.nutritionNote: per serving, rough estimate from standard ingredient values (not looked up one by one), without sides

recipes.title: Parmesan Cauliflower Florets
recipes.note: Party finger food for cocktails — about 8 nibble portions from one head. Oven-baked, mild, no heat. Garlic aioli is my own addition, replacing the source's jarred marinara.

ingredients.item: medium cauliflower, cut into bite-sized florets
ground almonds (or finely crushed pork rinds)

method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Line a baking tray with parchment.
Pat the florets completely dry, or the coating won't stick.
Put the beaten eggs in one bowl. Mix the ground almonds, Parmesan, herbs, salt and pepper in another.
Dip each floret in the egg, let the excess drip off, then press it into the crumb.
Space the florets out on the tray in a single layer so they roast rather than steam.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, until golden and tender inside. Cool briefly.
For the aioli: whisk the egg yolk, garlic, lemon juice, Dijon and salt. Slowly whisk in the olive oil, a thin trickle at first, until thick.
Serve the florets hot with the aioli.
notes: Makes about 8 nibble portions. Roughly 1 head per 6–8 guests.
Best hot: bake in two trays and hold the second batch back until the first is gone.
The aioli can be made up to a day ahead. Aioli is not in the source recipe.
Quantities converted from cups: 1 cup almond flour ≈ 100g, ½ cup Parmesan ≈ 50g.
recipes.nutritionNote: per serving, from the source's panel (not independently checked; aioli not included)

recipes.title: Creamy Mashed Potato with Nutmeg
recipes.note: Side for the lamb stew. Scaled from 1kg potatoes (serves 4-6) to 800g for 4.

ingredients.item: floury potatoes (Maris Piper), peeled and cut into even chunks

method: Put the potatoes in a large pan with a pinch of salt and cover with cold water. Bring to the boil, then simmer for about 25 minutes until tender.
Drain and return to the pan. Lay a clean tea towel over the top and put the lid on, so the steam is absorbed and the potatoes stay hot and dry.
Meanwhile, warm the milk, nutmeg, bay leaf and butter in a small pan until the butter has melted.
Mash the potatoes, then strain the warm milk mixture into them and beat with a wooden spoon until fluffy. Stir in the cream and serve.
notes: Peel and chop up to a few hours ahead: keep the pieces fully covered in cold water and cook them in the same water. Salt only when you're ready to boil.
Make-ahead: keeps covered in the fridge for up to 48 hours. Reheat covered in the microwave on medium for about 3 minutes, then rest for 1 minute.
recipes.nutritionNote: per serving, from the source (1kg potatoes for 4-6); about the same per portion at 800g for 4

recipes.title: Griddled Little Gem, Almond & Herb Salad
recipes.note: Side for the lamb stew. Lemon used instead of the white wine vinegar.

ingredients.item: dill, leaves chopped (keep a few fronds back)
lemon, zest and juice (instead of 1 tbsp white wine vinegar)

method: Chop the almonds and mix them in a bowl with the garlic, parsley, most of the dill, 6 tbsp olive oil, the lemon zest and juice, the sugar and plenty of salt and pepper.
Quarter each lettuce lengthways and brush the cut sides with the remaining 1 tbsp oil.
Heat a griddle or frying pan until hot. Cook the wedges cut-side down until well coloured but still crisp in the middle.
Arrange on a platter, spoon over the dressing and scatter with the reserved dill fronds.
notes: On a barbecue: sear the wedges briefly, turning from one cut side to the other.

recipes.title: Slow-Cooked Beef Shin in Ale
recipes.time: 25 mins prep + 3-4 hrs in the oven
recipes.note: Prep-ahead oven night: brown and assemble earlier in the day, then leave it in a low oven. Serve with the Creamy Mashed Potato (half quantity).

ingredients.item: boneless beef shin, in large pieces (or about 800g bone-in)
chicken or vegetable stock, roughly (enough to come three-quarters up the meat)
thyme sprig, plus extra leaves to finish

method: Earlier in the day: heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan, gas 3). Heat the oil in a small flameproof casserole with a tight-fitting lid over a medium heat. Season the beef and brown it on all sides.
Add the ale and enough stock to come about three-quarters of the way up the meat. Bring to the boil, then add the shallots, celery, parsnip, carrot, bay, rosemary and thyme. Season.
Cover and cook in the oven for 3-4 hours (4-5 if using bone-in), until the beef is falling apart. Check it after 3 hours if you're around; if it isn't tender, give it another 30 minutes.

At dinnertime: lift out the herb sprigs and rest the beef on a plate. Boil the liquid hard on the hob for a few minutes to reduce it, or thicken with a little cornflour mixed with some of the liquid, taking care not to break up the veg. Scatter with thyme leaves and serve with mash.
notes: Scaled from the source (2kg bone-in shin, 750ml ale, 250ml stock, serves 4-6) to 600g boneless for 2. The source says boneless shin needs 3-4 hours rather than 4-5.
Can be cooked up to 48 hours ahead: cool, chill, then reheat covered at 160°C (140°C fan) for 30-40 minutes until piping hot.

Nutrition worked out from per-ingredient USDA data on 2026-10-20, excluding the mash. Beef uses the lean-only shin entry, so real fat is probably a bit higher. The ale counts only its carbs and protein, because most of the alcohol cooks off. Stock and herbs are not counted.

recipes.title: Cider Pork with Apples
recipes.note: Serve with the Creamy Mashed Potato (half quantity). Start the potatoes first.

ingredients.item: small apples, peeled, cored and cut into wedges
A small handful of thyme leaves, chopped (keep some to garnish)

method: Heat the oil and butter in a frying pan. Season the chops and brown them for 3 minutes. Turn them over, add the apple wedges and cook until the apples are golden.
Pour in the cider and let it bubble for 8-10 minutes until the pork is cooked through. Move the pork and apples to a warm dish.
Stir the mustard, crème fraîche and most of the thyme into the pan. Bubble for about 2 minutes until it thickens, then spoon over the pork.
Scatter with the rest of the thyme and serve with mash.
notes: Nutrition worked out from per-ingredient data on 2026-10-20, excluding the mash. Assumes about 175g of chop each. The cider counts only its carbs. Mustard and thyme are not counted.
recipes.nutritionNote: per serving, estimated from the ingredients, without mash

recipes.title: Ale and Barley Lamb Shanks
recipes.time: 8 mins prep + 2 hrs 30 in the oven
recipes.note: Prep-ahead oven night: 8 mins hands-on, then it cooks itself. Umami paste swapped for tomato purée and white miso.

ingredients.item: large leek, halved, washed and roughly chopped

method: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan, gas 3).
Brown the lamb shanks all over in the olive oil in a large casserole over a high heat. While they brown, halve, wash and roughly chop the leek.
Add the leek, pearl barley, tomato purée, miso, salt and pepper to the casserole and stir.

Pour in the ale, vinegar and water, enough to just cover everything. Bring to a simmer, put the lid on and cook in the oven for 2 hours 30 minutes, until the lamb is falling off the bone and the barley is tender.
notes: Recipe as written serves 4 (4 shanks, 2 leeks, 200g barley, 500ml ale, 1.2 litres water); halved here for 2.

The source uses 1 heaped tbsp umami paste, a bottled paste. The tomato purée and miso swap is my own adaptation, not from the source, and the amounts are a first guess. Taste the broth before serving.

Nutrition worked out from per-ingredient USDA data on 2026-11-03, with the barley, leek and ale counted in full. It assumes about half the bone-in weight is edible meat (about 200g a person) and uses the whole-leg lean-and-fat entry for lamb, so it's a rough guide. The ale counts only its carbs and protein, because most of the alcohol cooks off. The source gives only percentage reference intakes, so there's no panel to compare.
recipes.nutritionNote: per serving, estimated from the ingredients as adapted

recipes.title: Sausage and Butter Bean Bake
recipes.note: One-pot with a herby Parmesan crumb. You need a hob-safe casserole that can go under the grill.

ingredients.item: chopped tomatoes with herbs and garlic (half a 400g tin)
olive oil, half for the sausages and half for the onion
mixed fresh herbs (rosemary, thyme, sage), chopped

method: Brown the sausages in half the oil in a large casserole over a medium heat, then set aside.
Soften the onion in the other half of the oil, covered, over a low heat for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for a few minutes more.

Add the vinegar, tomatoes, water and sugar, if using. Simmer for about 5 minutes to reduce, then stir in the butter beans, cherry tomatoes and sausages. Cook for 10-15 minutes until the sausages are cooked through.

Heat the grill to medium. Mix the breadcrumbs, herbs, Parmesan, oil, remaining garlic and salt. Scatter over the casserole and grill for about 5 minutes until golden. Or toast the crumb in a frying pan and spoon it over.
notes: Recipe as written serves 4 (8 sausages, 2 red onions, a full tin each of tomatoes and butter beans); halved here for 2. Half a tin of each is left over; keep it covered in the fridge for a day or two.

Nutrition worked out from per-ingredient USDA data on 2026-11-03. Sausages are assumed at 70g each and use the Italian pork sausage entry, which is fattier than most UK sausages, so treat the calories and fat as an upper bound: the real figure is probably nearer the source's 572 kcal. Butter beans use the cooked lima bean entry. Herbs, vinegar and water are not counted. The source panel (572 kcal, 36.5g carbs, 40g fat a serving) was not used.

recipes.title: Baked Cod with Potatoes and Tomatoes
recipes.note: Cod fillets or loin, skin on, from the fishmonger or fish counter (the sea bream from the freezer is gone). Fish is thicker than bream, so check it's opaque right through. Serve with green beans or tenderstem.

ingredients.item: baby new potatoes, halved if large
cod loin or thick fillets, skin on (2 pieces)
spring onions, trimmed and finely sliced
Flaked sea salt and black pepper
green beans or tenderstem broccoli, to serve

method: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan, gas 7). Boil the potatoes for 10 minutes and drain well.
Spread the potatoes on a baking sheet, lightly crush them, season and drizzle with 1 tsp of the oil. Bake for 20 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Meanwhile, score the fish skin three times if it has skin. Mix the lemon zest with the thyme, rub it into both sides of the fish and season lightly.

Scatter the spring onions and tomatoes over the potatoes and toss. Make gaps and place the fish skin-side up. Drizzle with the remaining oil and return to the oven for 12-15 minutes (thick cod loin may need the full 15), until the fish is cooked and the tomatoes have softened.
Finish with the lemon juice and serve with boiled green beans or tenderstem.
notes: Recipe as written serves 4 (500g potatoes, 600g fillets) and uses sea bream; halved here for 2. Swapped to cod on 2026-11-09 because the bream was no longer available — the source itself suggests cod or sea bass.
The source serves it with runner beans; green beans or tenderstem are the in-season swap and aren't on the panel.

Nutrition worked out from per-ingredient USDA data on 2026-11-03 using raw striped sea bass as a stand-in for bream, then adjusted on 2026-11-09 for raw Atlantic cod (cod values from memory, not re-looked-up, so treat as ~). Herbs and lemon are not counted.
recipes.nutritionNote: per serving, estimated from the ingredients as scaled, without the beans
